Group rows by keys

Source: R/grp.R
grp.Rd

grp() gives each row the identifier of its key's group, with the number of groups, each group's size, and the order that puts each group's rows together. It is the kernel the bracket's by runs on.

Usage

grp(..., sort = FALSE)

Arguments

...

Key vectors of one length (integer, double, logical, character, factor, integer64, or a list of raw vectors), or a data frame or list of them.

sort

Number the groups in key order rather than first appearance.

Value

A list: id (integer, 1-based), n, sizes, starts (into order), order (a permutation, stable within a group) and keys (the key columns, one row per group, in identifier order).

Details

Identifiers follow first appearance, so for one key grp(x)$id is match(x, unique(x)); with sort = TRUE they follow the keys' sort order, NA last, and g$keys is sorted. NA equals NA; for doubles NA and NaN are different keys and -0 equals 0. Strings are equal when their text is, whatever their encoding.

Examples

g <- grp(c("b", "a", "b", NA))
g$id
#> [1] 1 2 1 3
g$keys
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "b" "a" NA 
#> 
grp(c(2, 1, 2), c("x", "x", "y"), sort = TRUE)$id
#> [1] 2 1 3
